title: MariaDB Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the MariaDB course.

entries.name: Check your database session
entries.summary: A database client sends SQL to the MariaDB server.

example.code: SELECT VERSION() AS server_version,DATABASE() AS current_database;

entries.name: Create an InnoDB sample table
entries.summary: InnoDB is a storage engine that supports transactions and foreign keys.

example.code: CREATE TABLE cma_maria_books(id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,title VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,pages INT) ENGINE=InnoDB;

entries.name: Insert a row and read its id
entries.summary: After an insert in the same connection, LAST_INSERT_ID can report the automatically generated id.

example.code:
INSERT INTO cma_maria_books(title,pages) VALUES('Moon Trip',60);
SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID() AS new_book_id;

entries.name: Search a lowercase form
entries.summary: LOWER makes text lowercase for a comparison.

example.code: SELECT title FROM cma_maria_books WHERE LOWER(title) LIKE 'moon%';

entries.name: Take a sorted sample
entries.summary: ORDER BY arranges rows before LIMIT chooses a few.

example.code: SELECT title,pages FROM cma_maria_books ORDER BY pages,title LIMIT 3;

entries.name: Join grouped text
entries.summary: GROUP_CONCAT joins text values from a group into one string.

example.code:
WITH books AS (SELECT 'story' AS kind,'Moon Trip' AS title UNION ALL SELECT 'story','Tiny Seed')
SELECT kind,GROUP_CONCAT(title ORDER BY title SEPARATOR ', ') AS titles FROM books GROUP BY kind;

entries.name: Use a short recursive query
entries.summary: A recursive CTE can use earlier results to make later ones.

example.code: WITH RECURSIVE numbers(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1 FROM numbers WHERE n<4) SELECT n FROM numbers;

entries.name: Check JSON text
entries.summary: MariaDB can work with JSON text using JSON functions.

example.code: SELECT JSON_VALID('{"title":"Moon Trip"}') AS valid_json,JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT('{"title":"Moon Trip"}','$.title')) AS title;

entries.name: Handle a duplicate key deliberately
entries.summary: ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE changes a row when an insert meets an existing unique key.

entries.name: Undo row changes in a transaction
entries.summary: A transaction on InnoDB can undo row changes before they are committed.

entries.name: Inspect the actual table rules
entries.summary: SHOW CREATE TABLE prints the database's stored definition.

entries.name: Make a practice database backup
entries.summary: A logical dump writes SQL that can recreate database objects and rows.
